newsitem.title: CHINA: China to boost bad debt reserve for bankruptcies.
newsitem.headline: China to boost bad debt reserve for bankruptcies.

text.p: China plans to boost the size of its reserves for bad debts linked to bankruptcies to 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion) next year from 20 billion yuan this year, the International Business Daily said on Saturday.
The increased reserve was part of a programme to speed up the use of mergers and bankruptcies in the ailing state sector, the newspaper said.
Beijing has been struggling to make its inefficient state sector more competitive and stem losses of state-run companies.
China passed a bankruptcy law in 1988 and 1,692 companies declared bankruptcy in the first half of this year, more than double the number for the same period last year.
But it has tried to encourage mergers rather than bankruptcies for larger enterprises, fearing social unrest if factories are shut and workers lose their jobs.

Another official newspaper said on Saturday that the Anshan Iron and Steel Co, long seen as one of the nation's problem companies, had posted a profit of 278 million yuan in the first 10 months of this year by streamlining and upgrading technology. It had lost 200 million yuan in the first half of 1995. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
